name: Tent
desc: The little house of cloth you pitch in the wild, held by poles and pegs - a roof you carry on your back.
prose: You are a tent - the little house of cloth you pitch out in the wild, held up by poles and pegged tight to the ground. You flap in the wind and drum under the rain, while inside the campers lie snug in their sleeping bags by torchlight. Children make one of a sheet draped over chairs. You fold away into a bag no bigger than a cushion. You are a roof you can carry on your back, a home for a night under the open sky.

lines: A bright cloth flown upon a pole,
each country has its own design -
A long thin strip that's sticky on one side,
you tear it off the roll;
you mend a tear, you wrap a gift -
A little dial with a quivering arm,
the hiker reads it for the way -
A round metal pot with one long handle,
you boil the soup and porridge in it -
